title: Observing an unprotected shared counter
description: You can locate the shared update and compare the recorded count with its target.

steps.description: counter is a global integer shared by both workers. You set each worker's loop count with ITERATIONS.
increment repeatedly reads and writes counter in one C expression. You can see that this worker contains no synchronization around that shared access.

steps.question: Do the joins themselves protect each update inside increment?
steps.answer: No. They wait for completion after the workers start; the worker's read and write remain unprotected.

steps.description: The supplied run prints Final count: 1161395 (expected 2000000). You have an observed mismatch rather than a dependable count from this data-racing program.
